Registers a control-flow entry from a basic block into an existing drop-tree node after asserting the target node index is valid. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Lowers the deferred drop tree into MIR by first assigning basic blocks to drop nodes and then linking those blocks with drop or storage-dead control flow. It explicitly calls `impl DropTree::assign_blocks` and `impl DropTree::link_blocks`.

Determines which drop-tree nodes need their own MIR block, which storage-only nodes can share a predecessor’s block, allocates blocks for owned nodes, and wires external entry points into those blocks via the `DropTreeBuilder` hooks. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Emits the actual MIR for each assigned drop-tree block by creating `Drop` terminators for value drops and `StorageDead` statements plus `Goto` edges for storage drops, while skipping the synthetic root. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Creates an empty `Scopes` stack with no lexical scopes, no breakable scopes, no active if-then scope, and fresh drop trees for unwind and generator cleanup. It explicitly calls `impl DropTree::new` twice.

Pushes a new lexical scope record onto the scope stack, initializing its drop lists, moved-locals tracking, and cached cleanup blocks. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.
Pops and returns the top lexical scope, asserting that it matches the expected region scope. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.
Finds the last lexical scope on the stack matching a given region scope and reports a bug if none encloses the requested span. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.
Returns the region scope of the current top lexical scope, panicking if no scopes are present. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Executes a closure inside a new breakable scope, records deferred drop trees for `break` and optional `continue`, lowers those exits afterward, and merges the normal and break exits into a common target when both exist. It explicitly calls `impl<'tcx> Scopes<'tcx>::topmost` and `impl DropTree::new`.

Temporarily installs an `if-then` scope, runs the then-branch builder, lowers the deferred else-path drops afterward, and returns the resulting then and else entry blocks. It explicitly calls `impl DropTree::new`.

Runs a closure inside an optional lexical scope, pushing the scope before execution and popping it afterward only when a scope was provided. It explicitly calls `impl<'a, 'tcx> Builder<'a, 'tcx>::push_scope` and `impl<'a, 'tcx> Builder<'a, 'tcx>::pop_scope`.

Runs a closure inside a lexical scope while possibly creating a new source scope for explicit lint-root changes, then pushes the region scope, executes the body, pops the scope, and restores the previous source scope. It explicitly calls `impl<'a, 'tcx> Builder<'a, 'tcx>::new_source_scope`, `impl<'a, 'tcx> Builder<'a, 'tcx>::push_scope`, and `impl<'a, 'tcx> Builder<'a, 'tcx>::pop_scope`.
Forwards scope entry to the shared `Scopes` state, recording the current MIR source scope alongside the region scope. It explicitly calls `impl<'tcx> Scopes<'tcx>::push_scope`.

Leaves the current top scope by first emitting its drops for the supplied block and then removing the scope from the scope stack. It explicitly calls `impl<'a, 'tcx> Builder<'a, 'tcx>::leave_top_scope` and `impl<'tcx> Scopes<'tcx>::pop_scope`.

Builds MIR for `return`, `break`, or `continue` by resolving the target breakable scope, optionally evaluating and assigning the break value, scheduling all intervening scope drops into the target break/continue drop tree, and terminating the current block so the exit path can be linked later. It explicitly calls `impl<'a, 'tcx> Builder<'a, 'tcx>::add_dummy_assignment` when coverage instrumentation requires a dummy assignment, and calls `impl<'tcx> Scopes<'tcx>::scope_index` when translating lexical scopes into drop ranges.

Builds the deferred else-path exit for an `if`/`match`-style control-flow edge by finding the target lexical scope, collecting drops from inner scopes into the active `if_then_scope` drop tree, registering the current block as an entry, and installing a dummy terminator to be overwritten later. It explicitly calls `impl<'tcx> Scopes<'tcx>::scope_index`, `impl DropTree::add_drop`, and `impl DropTree::add_entry`.

Creates a fresh internal unit-typed temporary and assigns `()` to it so MIR contains a statement for coverage instrumentation on paths like `continue`. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Lowers all drops for the current top lexical scope on normal exit, first checking whether value drops require unwind cleanup and then building the scope’s drop sequence with the appropriate unwind/generator settings. It explicitly calls `impl Scope::needs_cleanup`.

Creates and returns a new MIR source scope inheriting parent lint-root and safety information unless explicit overrides are provided, and stores it in `self.source_scopes`. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.
Builds a `SourceInfo` value from the given span and the builder’s current source scope. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.
Returns the current lexical region scope for the builder. It explicitly calls `impl<'tcx> Scopes<'tcx>::topmost`.
Schedules both the storage cleanup and value drop for a local in the given region scope. It explicitly calls `impl<'a, 'tcx> Builder<'a, 'tcx>::schedule_drop` twice.

Schedules a deferred storage or value drop for a local in the appropriate lexical scope, skipping value drops for types that do not need dropping, validating storage drops for non-arguments, and invalidating cached cleanup paths in enclosing scopes before appending the new drop. It explicitly calls `impl Scope::invalidate_cache` on affected scopes.

Scans the given operands for `Operand::Move` values that are plain locals in the current top lexical scope, and records those locals in `scope.moved_locals` when that scope already has a `DropKind::Value` drop scheduled for them. It calls `Builder::local_scope` to verify it is operating on the topmost local scope.

Computes and caches the unwind drop-chain for the current scope stack by reusing the nearest `cached_unwind_block` and extending it with uncached scope drops. For each applicable drop it calls `DropTree::add_drop` on `self.scopes.unwind_drops`, including only `DropKind::Value` drops unless lowering a generator.

Registers the unwind cleanup path for a block whose terminator may unwind. It calls `Builder::diverge_cleanup` to obtain the current unwind drop node, then calls `DropTree::add_entry` on `self.scopes.unwind_drops` to connect `start` into that cleanup tree.

Computes and caches the generator-drop cleanup chain reachable from a `Yield` terminator by reusing the nearest `cached_generator_drop_block` and extending it with all drops from uncached scopes. It calls `DropTree::add_drop` on `self.scopes.generator_drops` for each scheduled drop, then calls `DropTree::add_entry` to attach the `yield_block` to the resulting generator-drop tree.

Emits a `DropAndReplace` terminator with a fresh normal-successor block, then wires the source block into unwind cleanup. It calls `Builder::source_info`, creates the successor block, calls `Builder::diverge_from` to register the unwind path, and returns the successor as `BlockAnd<()>`.

Emits an `Assert` terminator with a fresh success block and arranges for unwinding cleanup from the asserting block. It calls `Builder::source_info`, creates the success block, calls `Builder::diverge_from` to connect the block to the unwind drop tree, and returns the success block.

Clears all scheduled drops from the current top scope after checking the region matches, and invalidates that scope's cached cleanup links. It calls `Scope::invalidate_cache` after emptying `top_scope.drops`.

Lowers one lexical scope's scheduled drops into MIR blocks in reverse order, building the normal-exit chain and connecting value-drop unwind edges to the shared unwind drop tree while skipping moved locals on non-unwind paths. When handling `DropKind::Value` entries it calls `DropTree::add_entry` on `unwind_drops` to associate the current block with the next unwind target.

Builds MIR for a normal control-flow exit drop tree and then links any value-dropping nodes in that tree to the shared unwind cleanup tree. It calls `DropTree::build_mir` to materialize the exit tree, calls `Builder::diverge_cleanup` to get the unwind root when needed, and calls `DropTree::add_drop` plus `DropTree::add_entry` on `self.scopes.unwind_drops` to construct and attach corresponding unwind drop paths.

Finalizes deferred drop trees at the end of MIR construction by choosing the generator-specific or normal unwind lowering path. It calls `Builder::build_generator_drop_trees` when `generator_kind` is present; otherwise it calls `Builder::build_unwind_tree` on `self.scopes.unwind_drops`.

Builds all generator-related deferred cleanup graphs: the suspended-generator drop tree, the ordinary unwind tree, and the special unwind tree used while dropping a suspended generator. It calls `DropTree::build_mir` for `self.scopes.generator_drops`, then calls `Builder::build_unwind_tree` twice—first for `self.scopes.unwind_drops` and then for the generator drop tree after adding extra generator-drop unwind entry points.

Materializes an unwind drop tree into cleanup MIR blocks and ensures its root resumes unwinding if no shared resume block existed yet. It calls `DropTree::build_mir` to lower the tree and then emits a `Resume` terminator for the root block when initializing `resume_block`.
Creates a new ordinary MIR block for lowering an exit-scope drop node. It calls `CFG::start_new_block`.
Connects an exit-scope predecessor block to a drop-tree block by rewriting the predecessor terminator into `Goto { target: to }`. It does not call any other methods from the provided methods list.
Creates a new ordinary MIR block for lowering a generator-drop node. It calls `CFG::start_new_block`.

Connects a `Yield` terminator into the generator-drop tree by filling its `drop` target, and reports a bug if used from any non-`Yield` terminator. It does not call any other methods from the provided methods list.
Creates a new cleanup MIR block for lowering an unwind drop node. It calls `CFG::start_new_cleanup_block`.

Connects a terminator that can unwind to the given cleanup block by filling its unwind/cleanup target, and reports a bug for terminators that cannot unwind. It does not call any other methods from the provided methods list.

Computes effective lint-root HIR IDs for the current and parent nodes, using maximal coverage mode to keep the original IDs or otherwise calling `maybe_lint_level_root_bounded` for bounded lint-root discovery. If the roots differ, it creates and installs a new source scope by calling `new_source_scope` with an explicit lint level for the current root.

Walks upward from a HIR node to find the nearest lint-root boundary within the current owner, stopping at the builder's root, at a node with lint attributes, or when a cached ancestor is encountered. It queries HIR metadata via `hir`, `attrs`, and `parent_id`, checks lint attributes with `Level::from_attr`, and records successful root-to-owner results in the cache with `contains`/`insert`.

Builds or reuses the deferred unwind-drop chain needed when control diverges to a target scope. It first resolves the target scope index by calling `scope_index`, searches enclosing scopes for a cached unwind drop chain, and for uncached scopes extends that chain by calling `add_drop` on `self.scopes.unwind_drops` for each relevant drop before caching the resulting drop index on each scope.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_build/src/build/expr/: Lowers a THIR expression into an existing MIR destination `Place`, dispatching on `ExprKind` to build control flow, scopes, temporaries, assignments, and divergence handling. It recursively calls `expr_into_dest` for nested subexpressions and explicitly uses `source_info`, `in_scope`, `ast_block`, `match_expr`, `local_scope`, `is_let`, `new_source_scope`, `in_if_then_scope`, `then_else_break`, `push_assign_unit`, `start_new_block`, `goto`, `lower_let_expr`, `push_assign_constant`, `as_temp`, `terminate`, `as_local_operand`, `push_assign`, `in_breakable_scope`, `diverge_from`, `get_unit_temp`, `as_local_call_operand`, `record_operands_moved`, `is_ty_uninhabited_from`, and `as_read_only_place` to lower scopes/blocks, `if`/`match`, short-circuit boolean logic, loops, never-to-any coercions, and value writes into the destination.

Checks whether an expression is a `let`-condition form, recursively unwrapping `ExprKind::Scope` wrappers until it finds `ExprKind::Let` or another kind. It explicitly calls `is_let` recursively when the expression is wrapped in a scope.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/simplif: Runs the core CFG cleanup pipeline on a MIR body: it constructs a `CfgSimplifier` with `impl<'a, 'tcx> CfgSimplifier<'a, 'tcx>::new`, executes `impl<'a, 'tcx> CfgSimplifier<'a, 'tcx>::simplify`, then prunes unreachable blocks via `remove_dead_blocks`, and finally shrinks basic-block storage.
Returns the pass name as a borrowed view of the stored label. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Entry point for the `SimplifyCfg` MIR pass; logs the invocation and delegates all work to `simplify_cfg`.

Initializes a `CfgSimplifier` by computing predecessor counts for reachable blocks from a preorder traversal and then borrowing the body’s basic blocks mutably. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Performs iterative CFG simplification: first removes `Nop` statements with `impl<'a, 'tcx> CfgSimplifier<'a, 'tcx>::strip_nops`, then for each live block collapses successor goto chains with `impl<'a, 'tcx> CfgSimplifier<'a, 'tcx>::collapse_goto_chain`, simplifies degenerate switches with `impl<'a, 'tcx> CfgSimplifier<'a, 'tcx>::simplify_branch`, and merges single-predecessor goto successors with `impl<'a, 'tcx> CfgSimplifier<'a, 'tcx>::merge_successor` until a fixed point is reached.

Temporarily extracts and returns a terminator only when the target block is empty and consists solely of a `Goto`; otherwise returns `None`, including loop-entry cases where the terminator is already absent. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Collapses a chain of empty goto-only blocks so a successor points directly at the final destination, while restoring intermediate terminators and updating predecessor counts consistently. This method calls `impl<'a, 'tcx> CfgSimplifier<'a, 'tcx>::take_terminator_if_simple_goto` repeatedly to walk the chain.

If the current terminator is a `Goto` to a block with exactly one predecessor, replaces the current terminator with the successor’s terminator, records that successor for later statement splicing, and marks the merged block dead. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Rewrites a `SwitchInt` terminator into a `Goto` when all switch edges target the same block, adjusting predecessor counts to remove the redundant incoming edges. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Removes all `StatementKind::Nop` statements from every basic block before CFG restructuring begins. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Deletes unreachable basic blocks by computing reachability, compacting live blocks to the front, optionally preserving coverage metadata with `save_unreachable_coverage`, truncating dead tails, and remapping all terminator successors to the new block indices.

Preserves coverage information across dead-block removal by identifying inlined instances that still have live counters, nopping obsolete live-block coverage statements, collecting unreachable coverage regions for still-live instances, and re-emitting them as `Unreachable` coverage statements in the start block. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Enables the `SimplifyLocals` pass only when MIR optimization level is greater than zero. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Entry point for the local-simplification MIR pass; logs execution and delegates to `simplify_locals`.

Iteratively removes storage statements and definitions whose destination locals are no longer used, repeating until no more statements can be deleted. This method calls `impl UsedLocals::is_used` to test liveness and `impl UsedLocals::statement_removed` to decrement counts for each removed statement.

Shrinks the local-declaration set by first building use counts with `impl UsedLocals::new`, then iteratively deleting removable unused definitions with `remove_unused_definitions`, constructing a remapping with `make_local_map`, and finally rewriting local references if any locals were removed.

Builds the old-to-new local remapping by compacting all used locals to the front of `local_decls`, swapping declarations into place and truncating unused trailing entries. This method calls `impl UsedLocals::is_used` to decide which locals are retained.
Creates a `UsedLocals` analyzer with zeroed use counts, records the argument boundary, and populates counts by visiting the whole MIR body. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Reports whether a local must be retained, treating the return place and arguments as always used and otherwise checking for a nonzero recorded use count. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Updates use counts after a statement deletion by switching the visitor into decrement mode and revisiting the removed statement through `impl<'tcx> Visitor<'tcx> for UsedLocals::visit_statement`.

Processes the left-hand side of an assignment-like statement: indirect places are treated as ordinary uses, while direct definitions skip counting the base local and only visit projection operands. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Custom statement visitor for local-use analysis: it ignores nops and storage annotations, fully visits side-effecting statements, and for removable assignments or deinitialization-like statements counts only the relevant uses/definitions. This method calls `impl UsedLocals::visit_lhs` for assignment/deinitialization targets.
Adjusts a local’s use count during traversal, incrementing during normal analysis and decrementing when replaying a removed statement. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Returns the `TyCtxt` stored in the local-remapping visitor. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Rewrites each visited local in place according to the compacting map, assuming the local was retained. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Returns the pass-specific static name string for the current `SimplifyCfg` variant. It does not call other listed methods.

Simplifies a `SwitchInt` terminator by removing explicit switch arms whose target is identical to the `otherwise` target, then rebuilding the switch target table. It does not call other listed methods.

Finds unreachable empty non-cleanup blocks, and when more than one exists, rewrites all references to duplicate blocks to a single representative by visiting the body. This method explicitly calls `simplify_duplicate_switch_targets` indirectly through the visitor used during `visit_body`.
Returns the visitor's stored `TyCtxt`. It does not call other listed methods.

Rewrites terminator successor edges that point to duplicate unreachable blocks so they all target the canonical block, then normalizes any affected `SwitchInt` terminator. This method explicitly calls `simplify_duplicate_switch_targets`.
Returns the pass-specific static name string for the current `SimplifyLocals` variant. It does not call other listed methods.

Iteratively removes unused storage, assignment, discriminant, deinit, and nop statements until local-usage updates reach a fixed point, keeping MIR CFG structure intact. It does not call other listed methods.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/cleanup: Walks the MIR body after borrow checking and removes analysis-only artifacts: it iterates mutable basic blocks and statements, converts `AscribeUserType`, `FakeRead`, and shallow-borrow `Assign` statements into `Nop`, rewrites `FalseEdge`/`FalseUnwind` terminators into `Goto`, clears stored user type annotations, and drops `user_ty` from every local declaration. This method explicitly calls `as_mut`, `iter_mut`, `make_nop`, and `terminator_mut`, and also calls `clear` on `body.user_type_annotations.raw`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_build/src/thir/cx/exp: Stack-safe entry point for lowering one HIR expression to THIR. It calls `mirror_expr_inner` inside `ensure_sufficient_stack` to avoid deep-recursion stack overflow.
Lowers a slice of HIR expressions to THIR `ExprId`s by iterating over the slice and calling `mirror_expr_inner` for each element.

Performs the core lowering of one HIR expression: computes its temporary lifetime, builds the initial THIR node with `make_mirror_unadjusted`, applies every typeck adjustment by repeatedly calling `apply_adjustment`, then wraps the result in explicit scope and optional destruction-scope THIR nodes before storing it.

Converts a single type-checker `Adjustment` into the corresponding THIR form, handling pointer casts, `NeverToAny`, builtin and overloaded deref, and borrow/reference adjustments while refining spans for diagnostics. For overloaded deref cases it calls `overloaded_place`, and it also uses `to_borrow_kind` to translate mutability into THIR borrow kinds.

Lowers cast expressions, distinguishing coercion casts, array-to-pointer casts, ordinary casts, and enum-variant discriminant casts. It calls `mirror_expr` to lower the cast source in each produced THIR expression kind.

Builds the unadjusted THIR `Expr` for a HIR expression by pattern-matching over expression forms and lowering each case before later adjustment handling. Depending on the expression kind, it calls other lowering helpers including `mirror_exprs`, `mirror_expr`, `method_callee`, `mirror_expr_cast`, `convert_path_expr`, `convert_var`, `convert_arm`, `field_refs`, `capture_upvar`, `overloaded_operator`, and `overloaded_place`.

Constructs the THIR callee expression for a method or overloaded operator as a zero-sized function-definition literal. When no explicit overloaded callee is supplied, it calls `user_substs_applied_to_res` to preserve user-written substitutions.

Lowers a match arm into THIR by converting its pattern, optional guard, body, lint level, and scope. It calls `pattern_from_hir` for the arm pattern and `mirror_expr` for guard expressions and the arm body.

Lowers path expressions into the appropriate THIR form for functions, constructors, const params, constants, statics, and local variables. It calls `user_substs_applied_to_res` for callable/constant paths and `convert_var` for local or captured variable references.
Converts a variable HIR id into either a THIR `UpvarRef` or `VarRef` by checking whether the variable is mentioned as an upvar in the current closure body.
Builds a THIR call expression for an overloaded operator invocation. It calls `method_callee` to obtain the operator method callee, then packages the provided arguments into `ExprKind::Call`.

Builds the THIR for overloaded place expressions such as overloaded deref or indexing by calling the operator method and then wrapping the returned reference in a dereference. It calls `method_callee` to construct the overloaded method callee.

Reconstructs a captured closure place as a THIR expression by starting from the captured upvar base and replaying deref/field projections. It calls `convert_var` to create the base upvar expression before layering projections on top.

Lowers one closure capture into THIR, either reusing the captured place directly for by-value captures or wrapping it in a borrow for by-reference captures. It calls `convert_captured_hir_place` to build the underlying captured-place expression.
Lowers struct/union field initializers into THIR `FieldExpr` entries. It calls `mirror_expr` for each field value expression while computing the THIR field index.
Trait method contract for converting a mutability/auto-borrow description into a THIR `BorrowKind`.
Maps `AutoBorrowMutability` into the corresponding THIR `BorrowKind`, preserving whether two-phase borrowing is allowed for mutable autoborrows.
Maps HIR mutability into the corresponding THIR `BorrowKind`, producing mutable borrows without two-phase borrowing or shared borrows for immutable cases.
Translates a HIR binary operator kind into the matching THIR/MIR `BinOp`, rejecting unsupported operators with a bug.

Determines the canonical user type to attach to a resolved expression based on its `Res` kind. For callable defs and const-like defs, it calls `typeck_results`, then `user_provided_types`, `get`, `copied`, and `map` to retrieve the user-supplied type for the HIR id; for const constructors and `SelfCtor`, it explicitly calls `user_args_applied_to_ty_of_hir_id` and then `map` to box that type. It bugs on unexpected `Res` variants and returns the boxed canonical user type when found.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/check/re: Records a pattern binding's variable scope in the current `var_parent` scope, if one exists; it calls `record_var_scope` on the `ScopeTree` and otherwise does nothing for contexts like extern fn declarations.

Builds scope structure for a block by entering the block node/destructor scope, creating per-statement remainder scopes where needed (notably for `let-else`), visiting statements and the optional tail expression in precise order, and then restoring the prior context. It calls `enter_node_scope_with_dtor`, `enter_scope`, `visit_stmt`, and `visit_block`.

Creates the lexical scope for a match arm, marks the arm body and `if` guard as terminating scopes, walks the arm contents, and restores the previous context. It calls `enter_scope` and `intravisit::walk_arm`.

Registers a node scope for a pattern, records binding lifetimes for binding patterns, walks nested subpatterns, and advances the expression/pattern visitation counter. It calls `record_child_scope`, `record_var_lifetime`, and `intravisit::walk_pat`.

Marks a statement as a terminating scope, enters its node/destructor scopes so temporaries and destructors are bounded correctly, walks the statement, and then restores the previous parent scope. It calls `enter_node_scope_with_dtor` and `intravisit::walk_stmt`.

Classifies expressions into the scope/lifetime behavior needed for region resolution: it enters node/destructor scopes, marks conditionally or repeatedly evaluated subexpressions as terminating scopes, handles coroutine/yield fixups, recursively visits nested bodies and subexpressions, and restores the prior context afterward. It calls `enter_node_scope_with_dtor`, `visit_body`, `visit_expr`, `enter_scope`, and `intravisit::walk_expr`.

Applies let-initializer temporary lifetime extension rules by analyzing the pattern and initializer, recording rvalue lifetime candidates for borrow-like initializers, and then visiting the initializer and pattern. It calls `record_rvalue_scope_if_borrow_expr`, `is_binding_pat`, `record_rvalue_candidate`, `visit_expr`, and `visit_pat`.

Recursively checks whether a pattern contains any explicit by-reference binding that should trigger extended temporary lifetime behavior for let initializers. It calls itself recursively through nested pattern forms such as struct, slice, tuple, tuple-struct, or-pattern, and box patterns.

Recursively scans an expression for borrow-producing forms in let initializers and records rvalue lifetime candidates for borrowed subexpressions within the enclosing block scope. It calls itself recursively and uses `record_rvalue_candidate` to register borrow candidates.
Links a child scope to the current parent scope in the `ScopeTree` and returns the computed depth for that child. It calls `record_scope_parent`.
Enters a new current scope by recording it as a child of the current scope and updating the visitor context with its depth. It calls `record_child_scope`.
Enters the standard scope stack for a HIR node, first adding a destruction scope when the node was marked terminating and then adding the node scope itself. It calls `enter_scope`.
Visitor entry point for blocks that delegates block scope construction to `resolve_block`. It calls `resolve_block`.

Sets up and tears down body-local traversal state, creates call-site and argument scopes, visits parameters, then processes the body either as a normal function/closure expression or via let-style rvalue lifetime handling for non-function bodies. It calls `enter_scope`, `visit_pat`, `visit_expr`, and `resolve_local`.
Visitor entry point for match arms that delegates to `resolve_arm`. It calls `resolve_arm`.
Visitor entry point for patterns that delegates to `resolve_pat`. It calls `resolve_pat`.
Visitor entry point for statements that delegates to `resolve_stmt`. It calls `resolve_stmt`.
Visitor entry point for expressions that delegates to `resolve_expr`. It calls `resolve_expr`.
Visitor entry point for local bindings that delegates let/pattern lifetime analysis to `resolve_local`. It calls `resolve_local`.

Builds or reuses the region `ScopeTree` for the type-checking root of a body owner by creating a `RegionResolutionVisitor`, visiting the body when present, and arena-allocating the finished tree. It calls `visit_body` for local bodies.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/elabora: Coordinates the ElaborateDrops MIR pass: gathers move data, calls `remove_dead_unwinds` to prune no-op drop unwinds, builds initialized/uninitialized dataflow results, constructs an `ElaborateDropsCtxt`, calls `ElaborateDropsCtxt::elaborate` to generate the patch, then applies the patch and runs `deref_finder`.
Synchronizes both initialization cursors to just before a location by calling `seek_before_primary_effect` on `inits` and `uninits`.
Returns whether a move path may be initialized and may be uninitialized by calling `contains` on both `inits` and `uninits`.
Implements a no-op debug formatter that always returns `Ok(())`.
Returns the mutable MIR patch stored in the elaboration context.
Returns the MIR body from the elaboration context.
Returns the type context from the elaboration context.
Returns the parameter environment by calling `ElaborateDropsCtxt::param_env`.

Classifies a drop as `Dead`, `Static`, `Conditional`, or `Open` from initialization state. In shallow mode it calls `InitializationData::maybe_live_dead`; in deep mode it walks descendants with `on_all_drop_children_bits`, calling `tcx`, `body`, and `InitializationData::maybe_live_dead` for each child.

Clears synthesized drop flags for a path. In shallow mode it calls `ElaborateDropsCtxt::set_drop_flag`; in deep mode it walks descendants with `on_all_children_bits`, using `tcx`, `body`, `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data`, and `ElaborateDropsCtxt::set_drop_flag` on each child.
Finds the move-path child for a specific field by calling `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data` and `rustc_mir_dataflow::move_path_children_matching`.
Finds the move-path child for a specific array element constant index by calling `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data` and `rustc_mir_dataflow::move_path_children_matching`.
Finds the dereference child move path by calling `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data` and `rustc_mir_dataflow::move_path_children_matching`.
Finds the move-path child for a specific downcast variant by calling `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data` and `rustc_mir_dataflow::move_path_children_matching`.
Returns the operand used to read a synthesized drop flag by calling `ElaborateDropsCtxt::drop_flag` and mapping the resulting place to `Operand::Copy`.
